notes:
Lead background: inbound from quickstart signup (free credits) — wants hosted API, low friction. Small support SaaS (ticketing + knowledge base) looking to add a streaming assistant in their web app.

First contact: 2026-02-21 automated welcome + docs link. Customer attempted a quick integration using the JS SDK and streaming 'json' mode. Reported frequent JSON parse failures when using function calls.

Key customer quotes / paraphrases:
- "Most of the time we get a function_call but the arguments field is not parseable JSON — ends mid-string or has unescaped quotes."
- "Streaming is great but our client parser chokes at random boundaries. Is there a recommended framing?"

Observed symptoms (from their logs and our initial review):
- model returns event sequence containing function_call with arguments delivered across multiple stream chunks; their client concatenator is naive and sometimes injects extra whitespace/newlines.
- some function args include double quotes inside strings that are not escaped consistently (likely model output / tokenization boundary issue).
- when they switch to non-streamed (single response) function_call payloads look OK — points to streaming framing/assembly problem.
- occasional truncated payloads when network interruption + automatic reconnect triggers; no explicit end-of-message marker in their parser.

Attempted troubleshooting so far (timeline bullets):
- 2026-02-22: smoke test by customer (JS SDK) — opened RW-2345 describing parse errors.
- 2026-02-24: AE (Jordan) triaged; advised to capture raw stream and not post-process until fully received. Sent quickstart link + recommended streaming parser pattern.
- 2026-03-03: SE session (Priya) — recorded (ff_20260303_blueleaf_demo). SE reproduced partial parse error: function_call.arguments broken across two chunks where second chunk began with """" (unexpected).
- 2026-03-05: customer uploaded minimal repro (drive file). SE noted client concatenation added an extra newline which fooled their JSON.parse.
- 2026-03-07: performed controlled test against hosted API with chunk size simulation — confirmed model can emit JSON that spans chunks; recommended delimited framing and a safe concat strategy.

Customer requirements / acceptance criteria (short):
- streaming assistant with tool-calling (invoke internal knowledge_search API) that reliably receives full, parseable function arguments.
- latency target: <250ms first token for interactive UI, tail latency acceptable up to 1s for function payloads.
- cost sensitivity: low-medium (SMB budget). Prioritizes hosted API self-serve.
- security: SSO for admin console + audit logs; data not PII-heavy but prefer audit trail.

Technical notes / recommended config shared with customer:
- use streaming with explicit JSON framing: buffer until model emits finish event or explicit function_call end marker; avoid invoking JSON.parse on partial chunks.
- prefer function schema that tolerates optional fields; reduce strict "required" nested objects to avoid invalidation on small formatting issues.
- recommend using the Redwood streaming SDK helpers that emit complete events (see code snippet sent in drive doc).
- if using own parser, implement incremental JSON validator (recoverable) or collect until matching braces count for top-level args.
- advise rate limit headers might cause sudden 429-driven reconnects — ensure reconnect logic replays or resumes cleanly.

Open questions / customer asks:
- Do we guarantee that function_call.arguments will be a single valid JSON object in the final assembled stream? (Yes — but assembly must be done client-side when streaming.)
- Do you have SDK helpers for common client frameworks? (Provided: JS/TS helpers; sent links.)
- Any recommended server-side fallback if parsing repeatedly fails? (Can default to non-streaming single response, or route to hosted non-streaming model variant.)

Next steps (operational):
- 2026-03-11: SE to run one more repro with the customer's exact browser environment. Capture HAR + raw stream.
- 2026-03-15: follow-up call to confirm fix or demo non-stream fallback.

Notes / CRM style fragments:
- 'customer keen to keep hosted path' — wants minimal infra.
- 'likes cost transparency - asked about token accounting for streaming'
- 'blocked on JSON parse; internal dev says "if we can't parse reliably we won't ship"'

Suggested AE play: keep it low friction; offer sample code and a short POI (paid POC) if they want an SLA-ish run. Documented suggested fallback: toggle streaming off for tool-call endpoints while we harden client parser.
